thread:
noah: Hey all, first-week question. I'm running a one-off embed job from my laptop against ~40k docs. Using hosted sandbox key then started getting 429s after ~10 minutes. Error:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-type: token
retry-after: 30
```
Anyone know the fastest channel to request a temporary increase? I only need ~90 minutes to finish the run.

infra-bot: Reminder: sandbox keys have strict quotas. To request a temporary bump email infra@redwood.com with subject 'sandbox-temp-increase' and include: account id, token id (if known), total tokens, expected qps, duration, and cost center. Auto-approvals common for <=5M tokens & <=4h.

tara: Hi @noah, welcome! If you want lower friction, ops can issue an ephemeral token for ~2h. DM me the window + cost center and I'll create it. Ephemeral tokens are logged.

noah: Thanks @tara — can I post details here or DM?

devx-lena: DM is better for tokens. If you plan to upload data to S3, tag it non-public and set lifecycle 7d. Also sample locally first to make sure the pipeline runs.

sec-ash: Security note: don't put tokens in chat. If the data contains any customer PII, redact before upload. If unsure, mark it and we'll advise.

ops-ian: Ops also needs a charge code to attach to the bump. @noah, what's the cost center and rough token count?

noah: Cost center "product-protos". Estimated total tokens ~850k, peak ~12 qps, duration 1.5h.

tara: That looks fine. I'll issue an ephemeral token for tomorrow 08:30-10:00 PST and DM it to you. I'll also add a note to infra@redwood.com so it's recorded.

noah: Awesome — appreciate the quick help! :tada:
